title: Curvaceous, Crimped
summary: Most Toronto towers, like anywhere, are rectilinear in form, all right angles making for infinitely banal variations on the rectangle. Exceptions to the rule draw attention where they deviate from the expected, and a pair of those exceptions bookend the towers in this image: up close, the scoop-shaped north wall of Pinnacle Lakeside draws the eye along its sweeping, stepped curves, encouraging to spring past the hard corners of middle-ground boxes to land on the faceted folds of CIBC SQUARE's South Tower, each angled plane reflecting the subdued light a surroundings a uniquely.
